response.sql: SELECT r.raceId, r.name, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(res.laps), '') AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM races r LEFT JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId AND res.positionOrder > 12 AND NULLIF(TRIM(res.laps), '') IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.raceId, r.name ORDER BY avg_laps IS NULL, avg_laps DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: 'Back-of-the-field' means positionOrder strictly greater than 12 (positions 13 and below). The request says '12 as the cutoff' without saying whether 12 itself is included.
results.laps is stored as TEXT, so it is cast to REAL. Empty or whitespace-only values are treated as missing and excluded from the average, as are NULLs.

All races are listed, including those with no back-of-the-field results. These get a NULL average and sort last, as the request specifies. The back-of-the-field filter sits in the LEFT JOIN condition so it does not drop races.
Races are grouped by raceId and name, as requested. Because races.name is not unique on its own, grouping by both keeps the output one row per race.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is inclusive: back-of-the-field means positionOrder 12 or greater (positions 12 and below), with the same handling of missing laps and races without results placed last.
